sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 381 'Otank'.
sources.note: Entry gives names (Utanga, Otanga), location, population (2,000 1953 Bohannan; 2,500 SIL), classification, 'Source(s) TCNN project; Refs Survey: Rueck et al (2011)'. No wordlist, phonology or grammar reference; Rueck et al. 2011 has no entry in the Atlas bibliography (only Rueck, Yoder & Hannelova 2007, Jos ms.).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record otan1238 and reference records 579035 (Alyebo 2018) and 78922 (Blench 2016).
sources.note: Both references are typed 'a wordlist or less'; n descriptive refs = 0. Alyebo 2018 = MA thesis, University of Nigeria Nsukka, 172 pp., listed by Glottolog as an overview;comparative;wordlist, language code includes 'Utank = Otank [uta]'; Glottolog-internal PDF (hh) only, no URL.

Alternate names Itang, Itank, Otang, Otanga, Utanga, Utange, Utank; 15,000 (2006 SIL); 'Dialects None known. Lexical similarity: 70% with Tiv, 60% with Iceve-Maci, 50% with Evant, 40% with Mesaka and Eman'; used as L2 by Obanliku. No typological or phonological notes.

sources.citation: Luke Initiative for Scripture Translation. 2024. Itang [the Gospel of Luke in Otank (Itang)]. Abbreviation UTA; language Otank [uta]; publisher The Seed Company; (c)2024 Luke Initiative for Scripture Translation. Digital edition on YouVersion (bible.com version id 3998), book of Luke only (intro + 24 chapters).
sources.note: Scripture text only, no linguistic apparatus. The practical orthography writes seven vowels (a e ɛ i o ɔ u plus ǝ) and digraphs gh, sh, ts, kp, ngw, and carries no tone or accent diacritics anywhere in Luke 1 (0 combining marks in 8,380 characters), so it gives no prosodic information beyond showing that the orthography developers chose not to mark tone.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. New research on Tivoid and its place within Bantoid. Slides, Bantu 6 conference, Helsinki.
sources.note: Otank appears only in the language table (source ALCAM) and the Central Tivoid A lexical tables; the phonology slides repeat that modern phonologies exist only for Tiv, Esimbi and Ugare. No stress statement for any Tivoid language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2016; PDF dated 2011]. The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List. Circulation draft, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge. 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Otank stress or tone. Table 1 p.1: 'Otank (=Otanga) Nigeria 3000 ALCAM' (data = ALCAM 120-word survey list). Sec. 3 p.2: 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only three languages, Tiv, Esimbi and Ugarə.' The Otanga column in the comparative datasheets (Table 2) and Tables 3 and 5 (pp. 7-8) carries untone-marked forms only.

sources.citation: Starr, Alan & Clark Regnier. 2008 [survey 1990]. Tivoid Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-022. 52 pp.
sources.note: Otanga only in classification, lexicostatistic tables (e.g. Evand 70% with Otanga) and reported-comprehension tables; no phonology, no stress.

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: 'Cross River State, Obudu Division; Benue State, Katsina Ala Division, Mbaikyor District. 7,500 with Icheve (1963). Benue-Congo: Bantoid: Non-Bantu: Tiv-Batu group.' Index entry only (state/division, population where known, genetic classification, dialect list, scripture status); the survey has no phonological notes for any language; the words tone/stress/accent do not occur in the entries.
Stubs; only Ethnologue lexical-similarity figures and the Blench Atlas table. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Alyebo, Nelson Orkaan. 2018. Historicolinguistic study of convergence and divergence in the Tivoid languages phylum. MA thesis, University of Nigeria, Nsukka. 172 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only substantial work Glottolog lists for Otank (172 pp., Utank data alongside Tiv, Oliti, Ugare); a comparative study, but a 172-page thesis may contain a phonological sketch of each language including prosody. Glottolog holds a private PDF (hh).
